text: On November nineteenth, at eight PM India time, the company behind Claude goes public. A one point four trillion dollar IPO. Big opportunity, or big bubble?
Anthropic lists on the Nasdaq under the ticker A N T. Eight hundred twenty five million shares, priced between seventy and seventy eight dollars each.
At the top price, that raises about sixty four billion dollars. A giant IPO.
So what does it sell? Claude, an AI model that businesses and developers use for coding, writing and analysis, through apps and an API.

And the growth is wild. Revenue in the first half of 2026 was sixteen point three billion dollars, up from one point two billion a year earlier. Its run rate is now about eighty one billion dollars a year.

But here's the catch. The same filing shows a net loss of eighty point seven billion dollars. Most of it, seventy two billion, is a paper loss on convertible notes. But computing costs are huge, and still climbing fast.
And control stays with the founders. Seven co-founders keep fifty point one percent of the votes through one special share. Buyers own a piece, but not the steering wheel.
So, opportunity or bubble? At the top price, it's valued at about seventeen times its run rate. That's priced for huge growth. If growth slows, the price can fall hard.
Would you invest, or watch first? Tell me in the comments, and follow money in cloud. Education only, not investment advice.
